label: Insomnia
phenotype_definition: UK Biobank field 1200: usually having trouble falling asleep or waking during the night versus never/rarely or sometimes
source_note: Jansen 2019 Nat Genet — UKB-only public release without 23andMe
pop_prev_citation: Jansen et al. 2019 report frequent-insomnia prevalence of 28.3% in the exact UK Biobank stratum and 29.9% in the full study; DOI 10.1038/s41588-018-0333-3. K=0.30 is a rounded phenotype-matched frequent-complaint convention, not the prevalence of clinically diagnosed insomnia disorder.
rationale: UK Biobank trouble falling asleep or waking is a participant-reported symptom phenotype

label: Sleep duration (continuous)
phenotype_definition: Continuous self-reported sleep duration in hours
source_note: Dashti 2019 Nat Commun — UKB continuous sleep duration
rationale: Continuous sleep duration is self-reported in hours

label: Short sleep (<7 h)
phenotype_definition: Self-reported sleep duration <7 h; 7–8 h controls
source_note: Dashti 2019 Nat Commun — UKB short-sleep tail
pop_prev_citation: Dashti et al. 2019 report 106,192 short-sleep cases and 305,742 7–8 h controls in the exact unascertained UK Biobank analysis; DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-08917-4. K=0.25 is the rounded analyzed-category frequency (0.258), used as a phenotype-frequency convention rather than a general-population epidemiologic prevalence.
higher_value_interpretation: greater liability to reported sleep under 7 hours
rationale: Case status is defined from self-reported short sleep

label: Long sleep (>=9 h)
phenotype_definition: Self-reported sleep duration >=9 h; 7–8 h controls
source_note: Dashti 2019 Nat Commun — UKB long-sleep tail
pop_prev_citation: Dashti et al. 2019 report 34,184 long-sleep cases and 305,742 7–8 h controls in the exact unascertained UK Biobank analysis; DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-08917-4. K=0.10 is the rounded analyzed-category frequency (0.101), used as a phenotype-frequency convention rather than a general-population epidemiologic prevalence.
higher_value_interpretation: greater liability to reported sleep of at least 9 hours
rationale: Case status is defined from self-reported long sleep

label: Chronotype / morningness
phenotype_definition: Definitely or more a morning person versus definitely or more an evening person in UK Biobank field 1180
pop_prev_citation: Jones et al. 2019 report 252,287 morning-person cases and 150,908 evening-person controls for the exact UK Biobank binary analysis; DOI 10.1038/s41467-018-08259-7. K=0.63 is the rounded analyzed-category frequency (0.626) for a dichotomized preference phenotype, not a disease prevalence.
rationale: Morningness is a self-reported circadian-preference phenotype and is kept separate from generic subjective sleep

label: Daytime sleepiness
source_note: Wang 2019 Nat Commun — UKB daytime sleepiness
rationale: Daytime sleepiness is a participant-reported continuous phenotype

label: Daytime napping
source_note: Dashti 2021 Nat Commun — UKB daytime napping frequency

label: Habitual snoring
phenotype_definition: UK Biobank field 1210: yes versus no to whether a partner, close relative, or friend complains about the participant's snoring
source_note: Campos 2020 Nat Commun — UKB habitual snoring
pop_prev_citation: Campos et al. 2020 reports 37% prevalence in the analyzed UK Biobank European sample; cohort approximation for liability conversion, DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-14625-1
rationale: Snoring status is reported from a partner close relative or friend rather than measured clinically

label: Sleep apnea
phenotype_definition: FinnGen R9 G6_SLEEPAPNO: hospital-discharge or cause-of-death ICD-10 G47.3 / ICD-9 3472, with G6_NARCOCATA and G6_SLEEPDISOTH excluded from controls
pop_prev_citation: Campos et al. 2023 explicitly use a conservative sleep-apnea population prevalence of approximately 5% for power and liability interpretation; PMID 36525587, DOI 10.1093/sleep/zsac308. K=0.05 is an external obstructive-sleep-apnea GWAS convention because the FinnGen hospital-record case fraction is not a population prevalence.
rationale: FinnGen sleep-apnea status is based on hospital-discharge cause-of-death and diagnostic codes

source_note: Jones 2019 Nat Commun — GCST007803 European subset
rationale: Rank-normalized sleep efficiency is derived from wrist accelerometry
